title: Cryptographic Proof Bundler and Residency Reporter
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a modular service that assembles cryptographic evidence bundles for data residency and encryption policies and exposes a queryable reporting API. The service will integrate with our KMS/HSM event streams (rotation, import, compromise), the audit log, and retention engine to produce signed, time-stamped proofs that satisfy third-party auditors and internal compliance checks. Key goals: (1) deterministic bundle format for automated verification, (2) retention-aware exports that respect residency tags and deletion windows, (3) simulated rotation playbooks for validation, and (4) flexible delivery: S3/GCS export, signed webhook, or internal console viewer.
acceptance_criteria: Service can ingest rotation events from KMS/HSM and correlate with active key versions for a tenant

Generate signed evidence bundles (JWS) containing: bundle_id, region_tag, tenant_id, key_version, wrapped_fingerprint, rotation_event_id, evidence_items, retention_policy_snapshot, and service_signature
Bundles are persisted in residency-specific storage and are queryable by date range and key_version via reporting API
Retention engine enforces deletion windows: if retention policy triggers deletion, evidence bundles are marked and archived according to policy and cannot be exported past retention expiry
Simulated rotation runner can replay historical events to validate bundle generation for at least 90 days of event streams
End-to-end integration tests with staging KMS and HSM mocks, and a manual verification checklist for SOC/ISO auditors
comments: 2025-02-18 - MC: Created ticket and draft design. Core idea: one canonical signed bundle per rotation event that can be independently verified by auditors. Chose JWS over COSE for interoperability with auditor tooling.

2025-02-21 - LO: Spike results: staging KMS emits rotation events with id + timestamp + key metadata; HSM vendor exposes signing key_id but requires vendor-signed attestations for some keys. Need to add vendor attestation ingestion step.

2025-02-24 - MC: Design decision: bundles will include two signatures: (1) service_signature (signed by HSM signing-key configured per-region) and (2) vendor_attestation (base64 PEM provided by HSM vendor). This covers auditors who require vendor provenance.

2025-02-26 - LO: Implemented ingestion lambda + serializer. Integration test passes for KMS rotation -> bundle generation -> upload to residency S3 prefix. Wire format: compact JWS + attached JSON manifest. PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5482

2025-02-27 - Review (PM/Compliance): Need stronger indexing for retention queries and to capture retention_policy_snapshot at time of bundle creation. Added retention_policy_snapshot field to schema and updated tests.

2025-02-28 - LO: Discovered edge-case: cross-region key copies (replication) produce rotation events with duplicate key_version ids. Temporary mitigation: dedupe by (key_id, rotation_event_id, region_tag) and include replication_flag in bundle metadata. Follow-up: propose normalization upstream in key service (ENG-37001).

2025-03-01 - MC: Compliance asked for export parity: bundles must be exportable both as signed artifacts (for offline auditors) and via reporting API. Added endpoints /v1/reports/bundles and /v1/exports/signed-bundle. Performance note: bundle generation is I/O bound; plan to batch sign operations using HSM session pooling.

2025-03-02 - LO: Implemented simulated rotation runner that replays 90 days of events into the pipeline; created smoke tests for integrity check (verify JWS signature, vendor_attestation presence, retention snapshot). Next: load test with 10k rotation events in staging and measure latency and HSM QPS.

2025-03-02 - Compliance (Aisha Rivera): Requested retention-proof scenario where evidence must be redacted when retention deletes underlying artifacts. Design: bundle contains hashes of deleted artifacts and retention_policy_snapshot; actual artifacts removed, but the hash provides cryptographic proof that an object existed and was deleted according to policy. Need legal review for redaction language.
implementation_notes: Bundle schema v0.3 uses compact JWS: header includes alg=ES256, kid=hsm-key-id, typ=RB1

Manifest fields: bundle_id (uuid), created_at (iso8601), region_tag, tenant_id, key_id, key_version, wrapped_key_fingerprint (sha256), rotation_event_id, retention_policy_snapshot (json-string), evidence_items (list of item-hashes), replication_flag (boolean-string), vendor_attestation (base64), service_signature (JWS compact)
Export options: signed artifact (.jws), CMS-like archive (.tar.gz + signature), or API CSV for bulk index
Signing strategy: HSM session pooling to amortize handshake, ephemeral key-wrapping for playback verification, rotate HSM signing key per region every 6 months
Retention handling: evidence bundles inherit active retention policy at creation; retention-engine sets tombstone flags and triggers archival workflow (move to cold storage + mark export-disabled)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: HSM vendor attestation availability may lag rotation events -> Mitigation: allow 48h window to attach vendor attestation; mark bundle as "pending_attestation" and include retry/backfill worker
Risk: High HSM signing QPS under load -> Mitigation: use local asymmetric signing proxy with strictly-scoped ephemeral keys when allowed by compliance; fallback queue with rate-limiting and alerts
Risk: Cross-region replication causes duplicate bundles -> Mitigation: dedupe by (key_id, rotation_event_id, region_tag) and coordinate with key-service normalization
Risk: Retention deletion and audit expectations conflict -> Mitigation: consult legal, provide redaction + hashed-proof approach for deleted artifacts
